note: Eisenstein's own Table I (p. 174) prints it as the mean interpedicular width of the canal (I.P.) of his Caucasoid men. The level table read it from Chaudhary's Table II (p. 35), as its citation and its source_kind, secondary, say; Chaudhary's 20 means under Eisenstein's name are his Caucasoid and Zulu Negroid rows of both sexes, each the same as his, and leave out his Sotho Negroid rows.
